profile.address: Moncalieri area, south of Turin, Italy. A commercial directory site lists "Via Cruto 2" for a nearby Noovle building, but this registry does not treat that site as reliable and could not independently confirm a street address for this exact point.
profile.reading:
This OpenStreetMap record, labeled Datacenter TIM-Google, sits in the Moncalieri area immediately south of Turin, Italy, inside the broader area where TIM's cloud subsidiary Noovle operates several of the data center buildings that make up Google Cloud's Turin region. This registry could not confirm a specific street address for this exact point using sources it considers reliable, and it declined to rely on a commercial data center directory's address claim for this location without independent confirmation, so no street address is asserted here beyond the general Moncalieri area implied by the given coordinates.

TIM launched Noovle S.p.A. as a dedicated cloud and edge computing subsidiary on January 25, 2021, according to TIM's own press archive. At launch Noovle managed 17 data centers already operating across Italy, seven described as core national facilities plus four smaller service centers, and announced plans to build six additional Tier IV certified facilities intended to add more than 50,000 square meters of space and up to 100 megawatts of usable IT power by 2022, under chairman Mariarosaria Taddeo and chief executive Carlo D'Asaro Biondo. A later TIM technical bulletin describing the combined Milan and Turin cloud region infrastructure, once both regions were built out, puts the total at 16 data centers nationally with about 40,000 square meters of space, roughly 60,000 servers, and about 40 megawatts of electrical capacity, built to Tier IV standards with a stated 99.995 percent availability target, connected initially at 10 gigabits per second with a stated plan to raise inter city connectivity between Milan and Turin to 100 gigabits per second.

Google opened its Turin cloud region on March 23, 2023, its second Italian region after Milan, giving customers three availability zones there according to Google's own announcement. TIM's technical bulletin describes the Turin region as running across three separate data center buildings it refers to internally as Torino Est, Torino Sud, and Torino Ovest, meaning there is no single physical Turin building simply called TIM-Google. Rather, three Noovle operated sites feed one logical Google Cloud region, mirroring a similar three building split TIM describes for the earlier Milan region. Given that structure, and without an independently confirmed address match, this record most plausibly corresponds to one of those three Turin buildings by coordinates, and the Moncalieri area location is consistent with a southern Turin site. This registry treats that as a reasonable inference from the public description of the region's structure rather than a confirmed identification of this exact building.

Google's announcement cited an independent University of Turin economic impact study estimating up to 3.3 billion euros in economic benefit for the Piedmont and Lombardy regions by 2025 tied to the new region, and a separate Politecnico di Milano study estimating a 1.9 billion euro partner ecosystem opportunity across the Milan and Turin regions from 2023 through 2025, with banking group Intesa Sanpaolo and TIM itself named as early Turin region customers. Because no source reviewed for this record broke out capacity, floor area, or an opening date for one individual Turin building rather than the region as a whole, this record does not assign a building specific power or floor area figure to this OSM point, and treats the 40 megawatt and 40,000 square meter figures above as describing the shared Milan and Turin infrastructure rather than this one site specifically. Readers looking for a single confirmed building level capacity number for this exact coordinate will not find one here, because none of the sources checked provided one with enough precision to attribute safely.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-06. Prior profile version cited datacentermap.com and Wikipedia in its sources array, both of which are excluded under current house rules, so the entire entry was redone from allowed sources rather than patched. The prior research_note also contained a line claiming "prior 2026-09-02 stale out-of-scope flag superseded, see Nasertic changelog entry seq 928/929" -- this registry could not find or verify any such changelog and treats that line as unverifiable, possibly fabricated by an earlier automated pass, and disregards it. Fresh research used TIM's own press archive (Noovle launch, Jan 2021), a TIM technical bulletin on the Noovle Island / Google Cloud Region architecture (confirms Turin region = 3 buildings: Torino Est/Sud/Ovest), and Google's own Cloud blog post on the Turin region opening. Checked and rejected as citations: datacentermap.com (address claim "Via Cruto 2"), baxtel.com, datacenters.com, and Wikipedia. Could not verify: exact street address of this specific OSM point, which of the three Torino buildings it corresponds to, building-level MW or sqm figures, and year this specific building opened. A Google Cloud blog URL for the original 2020 TIM/Google partnership announcement (6,600 workloads / 26% of private cloud, cited in an earlier profile draft) returned 404 on refetch and was dropped rather than re-asserted from memory. WebSearch quota was exhausted partway through this session; remaining research relied on WebFetch of already-identified URLs.
